QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_11

question.text: The 'Clawback' provision in a Category II AIF's Contribution Agreement primarily protects:

answer.text: The manager from adverse tax assessments
Investors, by allowing recovery of incentive fees paid on early exits when subsequent investments fail

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Ch 9.3.2: Clawback entitles INVESTORS to reverse incentive fees taken by the manager during the fund life so that carried interest is paid only as per pre-determined total-profit ratio. Critical when early deals succeed and later deals fail. **The Trap:** Option A is unrelated. Option C describes Trustee indemnity clauses — a different PPM section. Option B describes Sponsor liability — different topic. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-A/B tests clawback as LP protection; XXI-B similar for PMS but rarer. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Clawback is only as good as the GP's balance sheet. LPs increasingly demand escrow arrangements or GP personal guarantees for X% of carry paid. As a GP, negotiate an interim clawback test at mid-life so no surprise at wind-up.
